previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and a history of mitral valve repair was admitted for acute kidney injury and fluid overload following a recent discharge. Despite initial management with diuretics, she remained refractory to treatment and required initiation of hemodialysis after tunneled line placement. Her hospital course was complicated by altered mental status due to hypoglycemia, elevated liver enzymes attributed to congestive hepatopathy, and a drug-related rash from fosfomycin, which improved with topical steroids. She completed treatment for C. difficile colitis, and her foot ulcers were debrided and showed signs of healing. She stabilized on dialysis, reached her dry weight of 77 kg, and was discharged to extended care with plans for vascular surgery follow-up, liver clinic evaluation, and continuation of wound and medication management.
